candidates.title: Test text rules for email sorting

demandEvidence.chore: Sort emails by whether their text contains configured terms, with a conditional route deciding the sorting outcome.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: the emails aren’t being sorted correctly

experimentPlan.output: A reviewed test report showing how configured text conditions route each synthetic email and which cases fail the expected category.
inputs: Synthetic expected route for each test message
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies a set of labeled synthetic messages and the text conditions intended to sort them.
steps: Record each synthetic message and its expected category.
Apply the operator's configured text condition to each message.
Use a conditional route to separate matching and nonmatching examples.
Compare the route result with the expected category.
List mismatches and ambiguous terms for a person to revise.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a labeled synthetic set, confirm every route result matches the expected category or is flagged as a mismatch, and ensure ambiguous examples are not silently assigned a confident category.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An operator must choose useful terms and categories, review mismatches, test with authorized messages, and approve any production change; no actual email account access or sorting deployment is established.
unverified: The n8n If node reference supports conditional comparisons only; it does not establish reliable email text matching or a complete email integration.
The post reports one current workflow problem, not recurring customer demand or willingness to pay.
No production examples or verified sorting accuracy are supplied.

ease.reason: A beginner can test synthetic text conditions; n8n documents conditional comparison routes, but not the email integration or reliable text recognition.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small teams sorting repeated email types might pay for setup help; this troubleshooting post establishes no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic rule test is feasible, and the If node supplies conditional comparison routing; actual email access and text matching accuracy remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: The If node can route based on configured comparisons, but a person must select terms, check mismatches and authorize changes to a live inbox.

evidence.reason: The native spans describe automatic email sorting and a text-match/conditional-node failure; the supplied n8n reference confirms conditional comparisons only.

candidates.reason: The fresh spans and assigned If-node documentation support a narrow synthetic sorting test, but this is one troubleshooting request and email matching remains unverified; provisional mean is below threshold.

candidates.title: Consolidate scattered trip details

demandEvidence.chore: Bring trip details scattered across a spreadsheet, airline apps, old inboxes and a photo library into one place.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: My trips were scattered across a spreadsheet, airline apps, old inboxes and a photo library, so I built Trvlrr to hold all of it.

experimentPlan.output: A single trip brief that organizes operator-supplied itinerary details and links, with uncertain or missing fields marked for review.
experimentPlan.trigger: A traveler or assistant supplies details for one upcoming trip that are currently spread across sample files and links.
steps: Collect only the selected trip's test materials.
Extract dates, locations, confirmation details and links into proposed fields.
Group extracted items by trip day and source.
Flag conflicting dates or missing details without guessing.
Prepare a compact trip brief for a person to check.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a synthetic packet with known dates and links, compare every proposed brief field with the input and require all conflicts or missing values to be flagged rather than filled in.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A traveler must provide lawful sample materials, verify each date and booking detail, and decide whether the brief is useful; the tool must not change bookings or access personal accounts.
unverified: No source documents an automated extraction capability.
The post does not establish recurring frequency, buyer intent or willingness to pay.
Privacy-safe handling of real travel confirmations is not assessed.

ease.reason: A student can organize operator-supplied sample itinerary text, but the post documents no extraction tools or workflow capability.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: frequent travelers or travel assistants might pay for trip organization; the post establishes no purchase intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can turn one supplied sample packet into a reviewed brief; source variety, accuracy and real account access remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: The proposed loop groups supplied details, but no automation is documented and a traveler must verify every extracted booking fact.

evidence.reason: The post explicitly describes trips scattered across four information sources and says its author built a place to hold them; frequency and outcomes are absent.

candidates.reason: Concrete consolidation task, but a proposed student organizer lacks implementation evidence and proven buyer demand; provisional mean is below threshold.

candidates.title: Coordinate booking and service alerts

demandEvidence.chore: Send booking confirmations, provider assignment notifications, payment status updates and customer alerts for an on-demand service application.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: How can n8n help automate booking confirmations, provider assignment notifications, payment status updates, and customer alerts?

experimentPlan.output: A proposed notification draft for one synthetic booking event, showing the recipient category, event status and message for human review.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator enters one synthetic booking status change into a test table.
steps: Read one synthetic status row.
Check whether the event is a booking, assignment or payment update.
Prepare the matching customer or provider message draft.
Mark duplicate test event identifiers so a second draft is not created.
Show the draft and event details to an operator for review.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Replay a small labeled set of synthetic status rows and confirm each produces only the intended draft, with duplicate event identifiers and unknown statuses visibly flagged.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An operator must define event meanings, validate payment and booking facts, approve recipients and messages, and authorize any real notification; no live payment or customer system is connected in this proposal.
unverified: No supplied reference supports booking, payment or notification integrations for this assignment.
The post does not establish event volume, field schema, failed-request behavior or duplicate controls in a working deployment.
External API access and real customer data permissions remain unresolved.

ease.reason: A synthetic status-to-draft test is scoping work, but no supplied implementation reference supports the requested integrations.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: on-demand service operators might pay for reliable booking updates; this request shows a need, not purchase intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic prototype can draft a few labeled event messages; external APIs, payment status correctness and production delivery are unsupported.

autonomy.reason: The proposed event-to-draft loop is repeatable, but no integration evidence is supplied and a person must verify facts and approve sends.

evidence.reason: The native post asks about four concrete notification tasks and mentions retries and duplicate notifications; it supplies no field details or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Concrete notification chores support a small mock, but there is no matching implementation reference and the honest provisional mean is below threshold.

candidates.title: Share received images with message handling

demandEvidence.chore: Handle customer Messenger messages containing text and images so the agent can use an image already received instead of asking the customer to resend it.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Even though the image has already been received and downloaded, the AI agent asks the customer to send the image again.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewed response draft that references an operator-provided message and the already supplied synthetic image description, while flagging missing image context.
inputs: Operator-written description of a synthetic product image
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits a test message marked as containing an image and includes its synthetic description.
steps: Accept the text and image-available label as one test record.
Keep the operator description linked to that record.
Draft a response using only the supplied text and description.
Flag when the image description is absent instead of asking for an already supplied image again.
Show the draft and linked inputs for human review.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Run labeled synthetic text-only and text-plus-image-description cases; verify the draft uses the supplied description when present and flags missing descriptions without claiming to inspect an image.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person must supply the image description, check product identification and reply accuracy, and approve any response; no live Messenger access, image processing or customer data handling is proposed as established capability.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference supports Messenger routing or image handling for this assignment.
Image interpretation is not tested or documented in supplied evidence.
The post establishes one reported workflow problem, not its recurrence or willingness to pay.

ease.reason: A student can test linked synthetic text and descriptions, but no supplied reference supports Messenger or image routing.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: service businesses handling image inquiries might pay for fewer repeated requests; this post establishes no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic draft test is possible, but live Messenger inputs and image interpretation are unsupported and would need separate validation.

autonomy.reason: The proposal only links supplied test inputs to a draft; a human describes images, checks the reply and approves sending.

evidence.reason: The native post describes text and image routes and the specific repeated-image problem, but gives no recurrence or outcome evidence.

candidates.reason: The post contains a specific workflow problem, but the available evidence cannot support the key Messenger or image capabilities; provisional mean is below threshold.

candidates.title: Review repeated Make data-sync failures

demandEvidence.chore: Investigate recurring workflow problems such as duplicate records or data not syncing correctly between services.

experimentPlan.output: A short review report for one operator-supplied sample failure, with the observed symptom, likely next check and unresolved cause separated.
inputs: Operator-supplied error text with personal data removed
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits one sample Make workflow issue for a bounded review.
steps: Record the expected and observed behavior from the supplied sample.
Separate the issue into missing, duplicate or failed data movement.
For a reported module error, list the documented Make error-handler option.
Draft a checklist of evidence still needed to identify a cause.
Return the report for a technician to verify and price.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Use labeled synthetic cases and check that each report preserves the stated symptom, does not claim an unverified root cause, and only mentions Make error handling for a module error.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A technician must inspect the actual scenario, confirm the cause, decide any repair and agree scope and price; the supplied Make reference documents error handling only, not deduplication or data-sync diagnosis.
unverified: The post offers paid help for smaller Make issues but does not document a specific client's repeated task or completed payment.
Make documentation supports handling module errors, not dedupe or data-sync correction.
No automated diagnosis, customer outcomes or recurring case volume is established.

ease.reason: A student can format a sample issue report; Make documents error handlers for module errors, but not the listed duplicate or sync causes.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small businesses with broken Make scenarios may pay for review; the post offers fixed-price help but records no purchase or buyer outcome.

feasibility.reason: A four-week sample report can be scoped, while diagnosing duplicates and sync failures requires workflow details beyond the documented error-handler capability.

autonomy.reason: The reference supports routing module errors to a configured handler; a technician must inspect the scenario and verify any proposed diagnosis.

evidence.reason: The post lists duplicate records and data-sync problems and offers fixed-price remote review, but provides no specific case detail or corroboration.

candidates.reason: There are concrete example failure categories and limited Make error-handling documentation, but no single case workflow or verified recurring demand; below threshold.

candidates.title: Review affordable AWS scaling options

demandEvidence.chore: Help a bootstrapped startup assess affordable AWS scaling options.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: If you are a bootstrapped startup and need to scale on AWS but can't afford it, reply with your email and I will help you out

experimentPlan.output: A comparison memo for operator-supplied sample AWS cost scenarios, with assumptions and questions for an infrastructure specialist clearly separated.
inputs: Synthetic monthly cost figures for a few operator-selected services
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies sample cost scenarios and a stated growth goal for a bootstrapped startup.
steps: Record the supplied cost figures, growth goal, budget ceiling, and assumptions.
Group costs by the operator-selected service labels without adding missing prices.
Compare the scenarios against the stated budget and goal.
Flag missing assumptions and any scenario that cannot be compared fairly.
Draft a short options memo for infrastructure review.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For synthetic scenarios with known totals and a stated budget, check that the memo reproduces each supplied figure, calculates only transparent comparisons, and flags missing assumptions instead of inventing savings or capacity.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A qualified operator must supply and verify current AWS prices, architecture assumptions, security constraints, and growth needs, then approve any change; this test does not access AWS or establish tax, billing, or production correctness.
unverified: No supplied reference documents AWS pricing analysis, architecture planning, or infrastructure integrations.
The post describes an offer of help but gives no cost inputs, workflow, recurrence, or outcomes.
Buyer willingness to pay and the usefulness of a comparison memo remain untested.

ease.reason: A beginner could format a cost-options memo from operator-supplied sample figures; no supplied source supports AWS cost analysis.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: bootstrapped startups seeking affordable AWS scaling might pay for advisory help; the request proves neither purchase intent nor payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can compare supplied cost scenarios and a growth goal, but the post gives no fields, constraints, or way to verify recommendations.

autonomy.reason: The proposed input-to-options memo is bounded, but no automated analysis is documented and an operator must verify costs and choices.

evidence.reason: The post requests affordable AWS scaling help, but supplies no task steps, inputs, recurrence, corroboration, or implementation evidence.

candidates.reason: Repair assessment of the named concrete AWS scaling request: a limited proposed cost-options memo can be tested with synthetic inputs, but no source supports AWS analysis and the honest provisional mean is below threshold.
